overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the chair may allow public comment on a noticed topic, public hearing law was outside review, and the council was only reminded to review complaints itself.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the council held an unnoticed public hearing by taking public comment on a bond order that was not advertised or posted as a hearing.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, the Council cannot violate the Open Meeting Law by allowing public comment on an item that was included on a meeting notice.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the public comment session violated public hearing law procedures for noticing and convening hearings.
allegations.key_passage: We do not review, and accordingly, offer no opinion on whether there was any violation of any public hearing law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the council authorized the city law department to respond to the OML complaint without first reviewing it as a public body.
allegations.key_passage: we remind the Council that the Open Meeting Law and the Attorney General's regulations require that the Council first review the Open Meeting Law complaint.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
